legacy_cells.B: HA-PI-MADT: A Hybrid Adaptive Multimodal Digital Twin-Inspired Framework for Reliable Healthcare Prediction with Improved Ranking and Calibration Performance
legacy_cells.C: M. A. Elsabagh; Rana Albelaihi; Esraa Hassan
legacy_cells.I: 079_2026_HA-PI-MADT A Hybrid Adaptive Multimodal Digital Twin-Inspired Framework for Reliable Healthcare Prediction with Improved Ranking and Calibration .pdf
legacy_cells.AI: Wearable physiological/behavioral sensor signals and derived features; tabular EHR/demographic data; statistical CT/MRI image descriptors; binary UCI diabetes risk-factor features
legacy_cells.AM: Modality-specific representations are scored with a lightweight relevance function, normalized over modalities, and combined by weighted-sum adaptive fusion; the paper also describes concatenation in preprocessing.
legacy_cells.DN: mental_health_wearable_data; EHR.csv; UCI_Diabetes_rows.csv; trainA + trainB (CT/MRI images)
legacy_cells.DQ: Wearable: 500 instances; EHR: 1,447 instances; UCI diabetes: 20 instances; CT/MRI: 1,742 training images and 744 test images
legacy_cells.EK: Modality ablations (all modalities, no EHR, no UCI, no image, wearable-only) and component ablations (without auxiliary modalities, deep branch, image memory, or stacking).
legacy_cells.EL: The DeepOnly variant showed sensitivity 1.0 and specificity 0.0, consistent with positive-class over-prediction; the authors also report sensitivity–specificity imbalance in ablations.
legacy_cells.FM: Proposes HA-PI-MADT, combining modality-aware adaptive fusion, multimodal representation learning, hybrid deep/ensemble stacking, and calibration-aware optimization for healthcare prediction.
legacy_cells.FN: The reported HA-PI-MADT results include AUPRC 0.6388, F1 0.6327, Brier score 0.2448, and NLL 0.6832; it did not have the lowest ECE (0.1388 versus 0.0641 for EarlyFusion_MLP).
legacy_cells.FO: The modalities are independently collected and not fully synchronized at the patient level; evaluation is described as mainly using a single train–test split; dataset size and sensitivity–specificity imbalance are limitations.
legacy_cells.FP: Authors propose validation on synchronized multimodal clinical cohorts and longitudinal trajectories, larger datasets, real-time synchronization, missing-modality support, and improved thresholding/cost-sensitive methods.
legacy_cells.FQ: The authors identify a gap in jointly addressing weak modality alignment, adaptive fusion, hybrid deep–ensemble learning, ranking-oriented evaluation, and calibration-aware reliability.
legacy_cells.FR: The paper supports static multimodal classification/risk prediction, not a world model: no persistent time-indexed state transition, action input, rollout, counterfactual comparison, or planning result is demonstrated. The authors themselves distinguish their digital twin-inspired approach from a strict patient-specific physiological twin.
legacy_cells.FT: A reusable static-prediction design lesson is to weight modality representations adaptively and report calibration alongside discrimination; this paper does not establish temporal dynamics or decision/planning utility.
legacy_cells.FX: Complete 34-page extracted PDF reviewed: title/abstract (p. 1); introduction and related work (pp. 2–7); methodology and preprocessing (pp. 8–17); experimental results, tables/figures, and ablations (pp. 17–30); discussion and conclusions/limitations (pp. 31–33); author, data-availability, and conflict statements (pp. 33–34). Read relevant Tables 1–11, including dataset, performance, cross-validation, and ablation tables. | Codex audit: title/byline, abstract/conclusion, targeted methods/results and cross-check of prior quotations against extracted full text. This is a targeted audit, not an independent re-extraction of every negative/unreported field.
legacy_cells.FZ: A:I left untouched as instructed. The paper uses a digital twin-inspired label but explicitly disclaims a strict physiological digital twin and reports static prediction rather than temporal/action modelling. Validation is described inconsistently: repeated stratified 5-fold cross-validation is reported in §4, while the limitations/conclusions describe evaluation as mainly based on a single train–test split; DU is therefore recorded as Multiple. The extracted text is readable; Table 3 has imperfect column alignment, so dataset counts are transcribed cautiously. KB §19.1 and §20 mapping references were not among the declared inputs, so FS and FU are omitted rather than guessed. Evidence QA: 29/37 populated fields had a <=25-word quotation matching extracted PDF text (78.4%). Confidence is conservative; review this row where exact quote checks were incomplete. Codex audit: 32 prior populated fields have a located source quotation; 5 have quotations not located by normalized text matching. Unlocated quotations are review flags, not proof that the value is false. Companion evidence audit lists affected columns. Reviewer FS/FT/FU mappings are synthesis. Prior unsupported/missing fields remain Not reported; no clinical benefit inferred from offline simulation.
